g.text: Data first, then metadata - so a crash leaves reclaimable garbage, never a dangling pointer
The API service never buffers a whole object: uploads stream through, so its memory is independent of object size.
1. DATA STORE - bytes written and confirmed durable FIRST
returns the object UUID only after the durability quorum acknowledges
A split-brain cluster map lets two halves place the same UUID - divergence no later
reconciliation can fix, because both are internally consistent. That is why consensus
is spent on a component touched by every write.
2. METADATA STORE - the row that NAMES those bytes, written LAST
Why that order, and not the reverse
data on disk nothing points at: invisible, reclaimed later by GC
reverse the order, crash -> DANGLING POINTER
a row promising an object whose bytes were never durably written
The user got a 200, sees the object listed, and gets a 500 or corrupt
data on read. Silent data loss reported as success. Unrecoverable.
Garbage is cheap; dangling pointers are data loss. The same rule recurs one layer down - a data node fsyncs the packed file
BEFORE recording the offset in its local index, so a crash there also leaves unreferenced bytes rather than a bad index entry.
Four background paths that are steady-state workload, not incident response
At 100 PB with a 0.81% annualized failure rate, drives are failing constantly. A design that treats repair as exceptional
cannot hold eleven nines - which is why repair gets a guaranteed I/O floor that user traffic cannot preempt.
